text:
Sean Gallagher: looping runtime folks in here. We need to tighten paging on TP hangs. Right now oncall can’t tell “slow” vs “stuck” and we either page too late or spam. Can we align on definitions + alert thresholds + immediate mitigations?

Rafael Mendes: +1. Specifically for Dedicated + large Hosted pools. What do we want to page on? request timeouts are too downstream.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. We’ve been using “no forward progress in TP group” as the primary signal in the scheduler, but not exposed well yet.

Omar El-Sayed: we can wire alerts off the new counters we added in staging:
- `tp_group_last_progress_seconds` (gauge, per tp_group)
- `tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total`
- `tp_collective_latency_ms` (histogram)
- `tp_scheduler_queue_delay_ms` (histogram)

Allison Grant: definitions first. if we don’t nail those we’ll keep chasing noise.

Sean Gallagher: propose:
- “slow” = progress happening but latency elevated (queue delay or collective p99 up), requests still completing.
- “stuck” = no progress at all in a TP group (no tokens emitted / no step completes) for > N seconds.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. The scheduler can observe “step completion” per group. For streaming, “no tokens emitted” is trickier because of client backpressure, but “no step completes” is reliable.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. what does “progress” mean in metric terms? token counters? step id?

Omar El-Sayed: current impl: each TP group increments a monotonic `tp_group_progress_seq` once per decode step (also during prefill chunks). watchdog uses time since last increment. So alert can be on `now - last_progress_ts`.

Tomáš Novák: for oncall runbook, need a single number like “TP group stalled > 90s” = page.

Sergio Costa: I can set up Datadog monitors but need concrete thresholds and “warn vs crit” behavior.

Sean Gallagher: thresholds suggestion (initial):
- warning: `tp_group_last_progress_seconds > 30s` for 3m (to catch early but not page)
- critical/page: `tp_group_last_progress_seconds > 90s` for 2m OR `tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total` increases by >= 3 in 10m in a pool

Rafael Mendes: 90s feels ok for Hosted where we expect steady decode. Dedicated customers sometimes run longer contexts though.

Sofia Ivanova: careful: long-prefill can legitimately go ~30-60s on big seqs (esp mixed batch) without decode steps completing, depending on how we chunk. In the hang cases we see *no completions* at all + queue builds.

Omar El-Sayed: we can split by phase:
- `tp_group_prefill_inflight` + `tp_group_decode_inflight`
- progress seq increments for both prefill chunks + decode steps, so long prefill still bumps progress if chunked.

Sofia Ivanova: right, but chunking isn’t always enabled for some kernels/configs. That’s why 30s warn might be noisy.

Sean Gallagher: ok. can we do:
- warn: > 60s for 5m
- crit: > 120s for 2m
for Dedicated
and keep tighter for Hosted?

Rafael Mendes: we can template monitors by “deployment_mode” tag.

Allison Grant: simplest: two tiers:
Hosted:
- warn: >45s for 5m
- crit: >90s for 2m
Dedicated:
- warn: >60s for 10m
- crit: >120s for 3m
Private (if we ever enable): start at Dedicated values.

Sergio Costa: works. We’ll tag `deployment_mode:hosted|dedicated|private` + `pool`.

Jacob Stein: also want to detect “slow comms” before stuck. we can alert on collective latency p99.

Rafael Mendes: yes, otherwise we only find out when it’s already dead. what’s a good p99 cutoff?

Omar El-Sayed: from recent incidents, NCCL stall signature had `tp_collective_latency_ms.p99` ramping from ~50-200ms to multiple seconds and then flatlines.

Sean Gallagher: proposal:
- “slow comms” alert (non-page): `tp_collective_latency_ms.p99 > 2000` for 10m (pool-level)
- page if combined with error rate OR progress stall.

Allison Grant: +1. “slow comms” should be ticket/notify not page, unless it hits customer SLO.

Tomáš Novák: for pager: keep it to “stuck group(s)” and “reset storm” (watchdog triggers).

Sofia Ivanova: define “reset storm”: > X quarantines/min? we should avoid paging on a single quarantine if it’s successfully isolating.

Rafael Mendes: right, single quarantine might be self-healing. repeated triggers indicates systemic issue.

Sean Gallagher: ok:
- page on `tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total` rate > 10 / 10m in a pool OR > 3 on same host (tag `node_id`) in 30m.

Sergio Costa: I’ll need metric tags for `node_id` then.

Omar El-Sayed: we have `node` tag in hosted; Dedicated uses `cluster_node`. I’ll normalize to `node_id` in the observability pack.

Incident Bot: Reminder: link runbooks in monitors. Current oncall doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/LLM+Runtime+Oncall (needs update)

Tomáš Novák: immediate mitigations section (what to do at 2am): can we align on safe actions?

Sofia Ivanova: from scheduler side:
1) quarantine TP group (stop scheduling new work onto it)
2) drain node if multiple groups on same node are stalled
3) shift traffic off pool if systemic

Rafael Mendes: can we do quarantine automatically on watchdog, but manual “drain pool” oncall?

Sofia Ivanova: yes. watchdog quarantine is in 1.19 hotfix path, but right now only behind flag.

Sean Gallagher: list explicit knobs for oncall to use now (pre-hotfix) please.

Omar El-Sayed: current mitigations we’ve used successfully:
- reduce concurrency: `RUNTIME_MAX_INFLIGHT_REQUESTS_PER_TP_GROUP` down 30-50%
- disable long streams temporarily: `STREAM_MAX_DURATION_S` lower (forces earlier termination)
- increase request timeout to avoid premature cancels causing barrier weirdness (counterintuitive but helped)
- set `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and ensure we’re not swallowing async errors (varies by env)
- if we suspect a single node: cordon/drain node in pool manager (Dedicated: remove from autoscaler target; Hosted: `poolctl drain --node <id>`)

Jacob Stein: and for suspected comm stall: flipping `REDWOOD_TP_COLLECTIVE_TIMEOUT_MS` from default 30s -> 60s can reduce false watchdog triggers, but risk is longer tail latency.

Allison Grant: we should be clear in runbook: increasing collective timeout is a *stability* lever (avoid premature abort) but can hide real stalls.

Rafael Mendes: also “disable TP” is nuclear. sometimes customers accept temporarily running smaller model / single GPU.

Sean Gallagher: agree but oncall needs permission boundaries. Hosted can route to non-TP variant if policy exists; Dedicated needs customer signoff.

Tomáš Novák: draft runbook decision tree:
A) Are we seeing `tp_group_last_progress_seconds` climbing for multiple groups?
- if 1-2 groups: quarantine/reset those groups (or drain node)
- if many groups across pool: shift traffic / reduce concurrency / consider rollback
B) Is `tp_collective_latency_ms.p99` elevated?
- yes => likely comm/network/driver; prefer traffic shift + drain suspect nodes
C) Is `tp_scheduler_queue_delay_ms` elevated but progress still happening?
- yes => slow, scale up / reduce inflight, not a hang

Sofia Ivanova: “reset those groups” is not always safe yet. today we can restart the worker process, which is disruptive. quarantine is safer.

Rafael Mendes: so for now:
- quarantine supported in staging only?

Sofia Ivanova: in prod, we have manual “remove worker from scheduler” endpoint (what oncall used in the Feb 13 incident). It’s basically quarantine.

Sean Gallagher: ok. Let’s name it consistently as “quarantine” in docs and map to whatever mechanism per env.

Datadog: Monitor suggestion from Sergio Costa: "[Hosted] TP group no-progress > 90s" (draft) created in folder "Runtime Stability".

Sergio Costa: I’ll hold off enabling until we confirm numbers.

Allison Grant: confirm final thresholds for first pass:
Hosted:
- warn: `tp_group_last_progress_seconds > 45` for 10m (no page)
- page: `tp_group_last_progress_seconds > 90` for 3m
Dedicated:
- warn: >60 for 15m
- page: >120 for 5m
Plus “reset storm” page:
- `tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total` rate >10/10m (pool)
Non-page notify:
- `tp_collective_latency_ms.p99 > 2000` for 10m

Sean Gallagher: works for me.

Rafael Mendes: +1. We can tune once we have a week of data.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll ensure metrics are emitted everywhere + tags. Also adding a log on stall detection:
`{"event":"tp_stall","tp_group":...,"node_id":...,"last_progress_s":...,"inflight_prefill":...,"inflight_decode":...}`
so oncall can correlate.

Tomáš Novák: I’ll update the oncall readiness doc + add “immediate mitigations” section with exact commands.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll post the scheduler endpoint for quarantine + expected side effects.

Sean Gallagher: action items:
- Omar: metric/tag parity + structured log (ETA?)
- Sergio: draft monitors w/ thresholds above + link runbook
- Tomáš: update runbook (include quarantine/drain steps + when to traffic shift)
- Sofia: document quarantine semantics + when it’s safe to restart workers

Rafael Mendes: also please add a note: “slow vs stuck” definitions in the runbook header. That’s what gets debated mid-incident.

Tomáš Novák: will do.

Sofia Ivanova: quick note: once watchdog/quarantine is default-on, we should change paging to be on “quarantine rate” rather than “stall seconds” (since stall should self-heal). but for now agree with current plan.

Sean Gallagher: yep, we’ll revisit post-1.19 rollout.

Sergio Costa: I’ll ping when monitors are ready in dd. :thumbsup:
